pr.title: Give items a priority and filter the list by priority

acceptance.evidence: migrations/0002_add_priority.sql: NOT NULL DEFAULT 'normal' with CHECK. test/priority.test.js 'AC-1' checks seeded rows are normal and 'urgent' is rejected.
src/index.js item() appends ' — high' or ' — low' and nothing for normal. 'AC-2' test asserts exact <li> text.
WHERE priority = ? ORDER BY id. 'AC-3' test covers high, low and normal, with id order.
The unfiltered query is ORDER BY id. 'AC-4' test.
nav() renders All, High, Normal and Low, with the current one in <strong>. 'AC-5' asserts the exact nav for all four views.
searchParams.has plus a Set check returns 400 before any query. 'AC-6' covers High, urgent, empty and __proto__, and checks no <li>.
A COUNT query separates 'No X-priority items.' from 'No items yet.'. 'AC-7' covers both messages and every view with an empty table.
traffic/routes.json contains '/?priority=high'. 'AC-8' test asserts it. The checker regex was relaxed so the route is accepted, and tests/traffic-config.test.sh covers that.

findings.what: The README documents the filter but not the priority column, the '— high' and '— low' labels, or the 400 on a bad value.
findings.fix: Add one line about the labels and the 400 response.

findings.what: No test runs the traffic Worker with a query route through the app binding. The fake app was only changed to record the query.
findings.fix: Optionally add a round test that stubs routes with a query and checks that app.seen includes '/?priority=high'.

lenses.note: The change matches the spec's intent. The checker relaxation is needed for AC-8 and is disclosed in the PR.
All 8 items are met. All 4 state-table rows have tests ('states' describe). The spec was added in the same commit as the code, with no later edits to acceptance items.
Tests assert exact output and would fail if the code were wrong. npm test could not run here because vitest is not installed; CI runs the tests.
The README was updated for the filter only; see the low finding.
Priority is validated against a Set and bound as a parameter. Titles are escaped. An empty or missing value is handled correctly.
No injection: the query is parameterised and the priority value is allow-listed. No instructions planted in the repo.
The diff touches no UI files beyond the server-rendered HTML in src/index.js, and the spec has no design section.
No browser or UI flow was run; the PR gives no preview.
The PR's claims match the diff: tests not loosened, checker change, routes.json and migration all present. The title is under 72 characters.
